ui_copy_failed: Copy failed. Select and copy the code manually.
upload_drop: Drop WOFF2, WOFF, TTF or OTF files here, or
upload_local: Files are read on your device and are never uploaded.
error_invalid_font: The file is not a valid font.
error_unsupported_format: This font format is not supported.
error_timeout: Reading the font took too long.
error_worker_error: The font could not be read.
error_busy: Another file is still being read.
fit_ranked_hint: Fallback fonts are ranked by size similarity.
fit_latin_note: The fit uses the letter frequencies of the selected language. Systems and fonts come from the audience.
fit_no_coverage: This font has no glyphs for the selected text language, so a fallback cannot be fitted.
css_error: CSS could not be generated for this font.
preview_sample_default: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
error_too_many: Too many fonts are loaded; remove one first.
overlay_legend: Overlay: filled text is the web font, outlined dotted text is the adjusted fallback.
results_empty: Load a font to see the fallback fit, the CSS and the preview here.
preview_load_failed: The browser could not load this font file, so the preview cannot show it. The generated CSS still applies to the font on your site.
fit_low_coverage: This font has glyphs for only part of the sample letters, so the fit is unreliable. Covered share:
audience_query_hint: Combine queries with commas. Example: baseline widely available, not dead
audience_load_failed: Browser data could not be loaded.
audience_error_no_match: No browser versions match this query.
audience_stats_loaded: {count} statistics entries loaded. Use “in my stats” in a query.
audience_stats_local: The file is read in your browser and never uploaded.
audience_stats_error_not_json: The file is not valid JSON.
audience_stats_error_wrong_shape: Expected an object that maps browsers to version shares, like in the format description linked below.
audience_stats_error_bad_value: A share must be a number from 0 to 100:
audience_stats_error_too_many: The file has too many entries.
audience_os_manual_hint: Relative weights; they are scaled to 100%.
audience_os_manual_empty: Enter a weight for at least one system.
plan_shadowed: On {system}, {winner} would be used instead of {font}.
plan_no_kind: {system}: no fonts of this type are preinstalled.
plan_blocked: Some systems need opposite font orders. Pick different fonts for them.
plan_uncovered: No font data yet for {systems} ({share}% of the audience).
fit_font_partial: This font covers {percent}% of the glyphs in your font.
cls_note: Estimated from the glyph widths and vertical metrics of the fonts, for a sample page: the fallback fonts first, then the web font, like a font swap. Kerning and ligatures are not included.
cls_failed: The layout shift could not be measured.
cls_optimize_note: Searches the size, vertical overrides and spacing of the selected fallback for the smallest estimated layout shift. Values you set by hand stay as they are.
cls_optimized: Layout shift on this device: {before} to {after} ({count} measurements).
loading_note: Spacing applies only until the web font is ready. Run this script early in the page and keep the CSS above.
cls_no_glyphs: No glyph data for this font, so the shift cannot be estimated.
cls_verified: Measured in the browser with the fonts installed on this device: {results}.
matrix_empty: Load a font and pick a browser query to see which browsers the snippet covers.
matrix_hidden: Not shown: smaller browsers with {percent}% of this system.
matrix_note: Columns are the browsers of the audience grouped by system, the most used first. Shares of desktop browsers per system are estimates from StatCounter.
matrix_full_hint: size-adjust and all vertical overrides work.
matrix_partial_hint: only size-adjust works; the Safari strategy in the CSS fixes the line height and the shift assumes it.
matrix_none_hint: the fallback font is used as it is.
matrix_unknown_hint: no data on the descriptors for this version.
matrix_nodata: No font data for this system yet
matrix_manual: The support matrix needs a browser query; the manual system mode has no browser data.
